title: Construct anchor file (v1)
description: JSON Schema for src/config/_anchors/<construct>.yml. Each anchor file declares a construct, names a single anchor variable whose direction is known and stable, and lists every variable expected to load on that anchor with a substantive justification. The Layer 4 audit diagnostic uses this file to mechanically check that every YAML's reverse-coding decision produced a variable whose correlation with the anchor has the theoretically-expected sign. The headline guarantee is additionalProperties: false at every object level so typos like 'expected_sigm:' or 'loadrs:' fail loud.

schema_version.description: Schema version. Must be the integer 1 for this revision.

construct.description: Snake-case name of the construct (e.g. democratic_attitudes, institutional_trust, economic_evaluations).

description.description: Free-text paragraph describing what the construct is and why these loaders cohere.

last_reviewed.description: ISO-8601 calendar date (YYYY-MM-DD) of the last human review of this file's expected_sign assignments.

waveKey.description: Wave identifier. Surveys use heterogeneous conventions (w1, y1995, r5, w2003, w2025).

varId.description: Snake-case variable id, matching an `id:` declared in some harmonization YAML.

directionEnum.description: Direction of the anchor variable itself. positive = higher values mean more of the construct; negative = higher values mean less; none = orthogonal or undefined.

signEnum.description: Expected sign of a loader's correlation with the anchor. positive/negative are theory-driven predictions; either is for ambivalent or multi-dimensional items where theory does not commit.

anchorBlock.description: The anchor variable for this construct. The anchor is the one item whose direction is known and stable; every loader's expected_sign is interpreted relative to this anchor's direction.

per_wave.description: Optional override mapping wave-key -> direction. Use when the anchor itself reverses direction across waves (e.g. question rephrased in W4). Per-wave entries override the global expected_direction for those waves only.

loader.description: One variable expected to covary with the anchor in a theoretically-predictable direction.

justification.description: One-sentence substantive justification (10-500 chars) citing literature OR codebook semantics. NOT tautological: 'they're related' is rejected on review even though the schema accepts it. Forces the author to write a real reason that an audit reviewer can evaluate.

min_correlation.description: Loaders with |observed_correlation| below this threshold fire a 'weak loader' warning rather than a sign-disagreement error. Defaults to 0.05 in the diagnostic if omitted.

surveys.description: Optional list of survey-name strings that restrict this loader to certain surveys. Use for cross-survey constructs where the loader exists only in some surveys (e.g. KGSS conf_* trust variables alongside ABS trust_*). Diagnostic skips this loader for surveys not in the list. Accepts a scalar string OR an array; jsonlite::toJSON(auto_unbox=TRUE) collapses length-1 arrays to scalars and the schema must accept both shapes.

waves.description: Optional list of wave keys that restrict this loader to certain waves. Use when a loader's theoretical direction is only meaningful in some waves (e.g. a battery introduced in W3). Accepts a scalar wave-key OR an array (same auto_unbox tolerance).
